Young Men’s Christian Association of Montreal 


NEWS LETTER 
March 27, 1969. 


GETTING DOWN TO CASES: Ways tn which youth and adults can 
become more equal partners in the search for answers to contem- 
porary problems will be high on the agenda of a Young Members' 
Forum to be held this summer at Nottingham University, England. 
An internattonal event, it will be correlated with the 5th World 
Council of YMCAs. 

Both global assemblies will jointly and separately re-examine 
the world-wide role of the YMCA today. Topics will inelude the 
effects of technological advances and inereased urbanization, 
inter-fatth and international relationships, communications and 
posstble areas of greater co-operation. 

Susan Young will represent the YMCAs of Canada at the Forum. 
A second-year fellowship student at Sir George Williams Univer- 
stty, she also works part time in WESTMOUNT BRANCH'S Youth 
Department. James G. Kendrick, President of Zeller's, will be 
the MONTREAL YMCA's delegate at the World Council. 


GOVERNMENT LANGUAGE CLASSES AT INTERNATIONAL Y: Under an agreement 
with the Quebec Ministry of Education, a "Centre d'Orientatton et de 
Formation des Immigrants" has been establIshed In INTERNATIONAL BRANCH. 
About I2 such centers are now operating In this province to assist in 
the assimilation of new Canadians. 

As Its share of this program, International is currently conducting 
seven classes for 105 students. Enrolment will be increased to 150 
when three classes are added after renovations to the building are 
completed. 


BUSY CAMPING SEASON EXPECTED: Pre-registration for the 
upcoming summer at Kanawana remains well ahead of last year. 
The Kamp's Olga Hall reports that as of March 26, the total of 
camper weeks booked stood at 420. 


TALENT IS WHERE YOU FIND IT: In bygone days, aspiring thesplans used 
to hold all sorts of jobs while awaiting their big break. They 
presided over soda fountains, clerked in department stores, walted on 
tables or worked as laborers, ushers or parking lot attendants. 

Ken McAuslan of DOWNTOWN BRANCH'S phys. ed. department broke Into 
acting the easy way--while practising his chosen profession on the 

gym floor. He was 'discovered' just over a year ago by producer- 
director Mike Sinelnikoff, a participant in one of his fitness classes. 
Since that time, Ken has co-starred in two CBC Teleplay productions, 
"The Sound of Goodbye" and "The Triumph of the Egg".

SHARPENING PERCEPTIONS AT NORTHMOUNT: Most people get the feeling 
sometimes that they are missing something worthwhile because they 
don't quite perceive or understand what is happening. At such times, 
they see others coping with and enjoying situations which they find 


dull or meaningless. 
Bill Horan of NORTHMOUNT BRANCH has developed a program to help people 
strengthen the sort of self-awareness which will sharpen their per- 


ception and enable them to enjoy more things. 

Key to the program is a series of exercises. These are done in a 
group, with participants objectively testing and comparing their own 
motivation and reactions against those of others. 


HAPPENINGS AT NDG: A WATER SHOW involving 100 youngsters tn 
an aquatic presentation of the elasste fatry tale "The Frog 
Prince". They're still trying to decide who enjoyed tt more-- 
the audience or the partictpants...A RUMMAGE SALE by the branch's 
Y's Mens Club. This was an all-male effort...Progress tn FAMILY 
LIFE EDUCATION; one program for parents of 3-5 year olds and 
another for those with children age 6-9. Final touches are also 
being put to a Parent-Teens Communication program. 


CAMPAIGN PROGRESS: Though many hundreds of prospects have still to 
be heard from, the MONTREAL YMCA's Financial Campaign reached 
$268,117 on March 25. This was equal to 71.5% of the $375,000 Metro- 
politan objective.
